reasons: We represent IBM, which is the Customer/buyer here; every audit, inspection and verification right in the cited paragraphs (Section 7.0 process audits, Attachment 6 §4.0 books-and-records audits, cost-shifting only on material discrepancy) runs in IBM's favour against MSL, the supplier.

No audit, inspection or verification right binding the Customer was identified, so there is no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access exposure for the rule to constrain; treating this as a deviation or missing clause would incorrectly attack a protection we benefit from.
Consistent with a compliant finding, the rendered redline is identical to the original paragraphs and no counterparty comment is proposed, so nothing actionable is required.
The failed 'audit frequency limited' deterministic check is a false signal here: the semiannual cap in p1448 does exist and, in any event, applies to audits of MSL rather than of us.
